items.title: Do you verify AI-generated content before publishing?
items.raw_excerpt:
I'm researching content repurposing tools and trying to understand a workflow gap: When you use AI to turn podcasts/interviews/webinars into social posts, do you verify accuracy before publishing? Context: Tools like Castmagic and Descript are 85-95% accurate. That 5-15% error rate means AI sometimes:
- Misquotes speakers
- Paraphrases in ways that change meaning
- Attributes quotes to wrong person (multi-speaker issue) I've found two camps: Camp A: "I carefully verify everything"
- Re-read transcripts or scrub audio
- Takes 20-30 minutes per post
- Zero tolerance for publishing errors Camp B: "I trust AI and publish"
- "Good enough" for social media
- Errors are rare enough to accept
- Speed > perfection My questions:
1. Which camp are you in?
2. If Camp A: what's your verification workfl

excerpt_i18n.en: On January 28, WeRide (NASDAQ: WRD, HKEX: 0800), a global leader in autonomous driving technology, officially launched its self-developed general simulation model—WeRide GENESIS. This model bridges Physical AI and Generative AI, connecting the real physical world with the virtual simulation world, thereby accelerating the large-scale R&D, training, and commercial deployment of autonomous vehicles. On January 27, 2026, the Tencent Tech for Good Innovation Festival (2026), hosted by Tencent Research Institute, was held in Shenzhen. On January 26, Alibaba officially launched its flagship reasoning model Qwen3-Max-Thinking, setting several new global records in authoritative evaluations. Its performance rivals that of GPT-5.2 and Gemini 3 Pro, making it the strongest domestic AI large model to date, closest to international top-tier models. Through extreme scaling in total parameters, reinforcement learning, and reasoning computation, the new Qwen model achieved a significant leap in performance, breaking global records in key benchmarks such as scientific knowledge (GPQA Diamond), mathematical reasoning (IMO-AnswerBench), and code programming (LiveCodeBench).  

Qwen3-Max-Thinking is currently Alibaba's largest and most capable Qwen reasoning model, with total parameters exceeding one trillion (1T) and pre-training data amounting to 36T tokens. Previously, the preview version of Qwen3-Max-Thinking achieved the first domestic double perfect scores in mathematical reasoning benchmarks AIME 25 and HMMT 25, showcasing impressive reasoning capabilities. Building on this, Alibaba's Tongyi team conducted larger-scale reinforcement learning post-training, comprehensively enhancing the performance of the official Qwen3-Max-Thinking. Across 19 recognized large model benchmarks covering factual knowledge, complex reasoning, instruction following, human preference alignment, and Agent capabilities, the flagship Qwen reasoning model set several new state-of-the-art (SOTA) records.

In 2025, China's smart glasses market is experiencing pre-breakout turbulence. Data from the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology shows that shipments in the first three quarters exceeded 1.78 million units, representing a several-fold increase compared to 2024. The annual sales of 2 million units for Meta Ray-Ban's camera glasses validate the market's potential. Companies like Xiaomi and Li Auto have entered the fray, but the industry is mired in a collective dilemma: consumers are forced to choose among audio, camera, and display glasses, with newly purchased devices quickly becoming obsolete due to rapid technological iteration. Manufacturers are obsessed with a lightweight race, yet trapped in the impossible triangle of "lightweight, strong performance, and long battery life." Just as the entire industry is caught in a cycle of "innovation for innovation's sake," Xuanjing unveiled a potential breakthrough at its Tech Open Day. Its M6 series breaks the boundaries of product form with a "magnetic modular" design, redefines user experience logic with "active AI interaction," and challenges the industry's decade-old iron law of iteration with the concept of "one purchase, perpetual upgrades."

Modularity rewrites the rules of iteration. "Users don’t want three functionally fragmented glasses, but a solution that can be combined and freely upgraded as needed," said Xie Xin, Vice President of Xuanjing, capturing the original intent of modular design. In April 2025, Xuanjing launched the ultra-lightweight M5 clip-on AR glasses weighing 25.8 grams. Its "zero-barrier" design, compatible with prescription glasses, topped three major JD.com charts within four hours of release, reinforcing the team's commitment to modularity.

Las gafas con cámara Meta Ray-Ban, con ventas anuales de 2 millones de unidades, confirman el potencial del mercado. Fabricantes como Xiaomi y Li Auto se han sumado al sector, pero la industria enfrenta un dilema colectivo: los consumidores se ven obligados a elegir entre gafas de audio, de cámara o con pantalla, y los dispositivos recién adquiridos pronto quedan obsoletos por la rápida evolución tecnológica, convirtiéndose en "chatarra electrónica". Los fabricantes, obsesionados con la competencia por la ligereza, caen en el trilema imposible de "ligereza, alto rendimiento y larga duración de la batería". Mientras toda la industria se debate en la "innovación por innovar".

The industry previously focused more on model performance in standardized tasks, knowledge Q&A, and literature summarization, but these capabilities essentially remain forms of information processing—they can enhance efficiency but hardly alter the fundamental approach to scientific research. The core challenge in real-world research lies not in the strength of isolated capabilities, but in the inherently long-chain, uncertain, and validation-dependent closed-loop nature of the research process. A seemingly simple physics problem often requires a full workflow: model selection, derivation pathways, numerical experiment design, code implementation, parameter tuning and debugging, benchmarking against reference results, and error source analysis. Any misstep can invalidate the conclusions. excerpt_i18n.es: Cuando las capacidades de los grandes modelos evolucionan de responder preguntas a completar tareas, la IA para la Ciencia también está experimentando una transformación más profunda. Anteriormente, la industria se centraba más en el rendimiento de los modelos en preguntas estándar, respuestas de conocimiento y resúmenes de literatura, pero estas habilidades pertenecen esencialmente al procesamiento de información; pueden mejorar la eficiencia, pero difícilmente cambian verdaderamente la forma en que avanza la investigación científica. La dificultad central de la investigación real no radica en si una habilidad puntual es fuerte, sino en que el proceso de investigación es inherentemente un sistema cerrado de cadena larga, incierto y fuertemente dependiente de la verificación.
